title: Ireland Extension
description: Irish succession law — Succession Act 1965, spouse legal right share, Section 117 moral duty provision, Capital Acquisitions Tax, intestacy distribution, dwelling house exemption, civil partnership provisions
$comment: Ireland does NOT distinguish whole blood from half blood. Siblings and their issue inherit equally regardless of blood degree.

spouseLegalRightShare.description: Spouse legal right share under Succession Act 1965 s.111 — 1/3 with children, 1/2 without. Cannot be defeated by will.

renounced.description: Whether spouse has renounced their legal right share

section117Claim.description: Section 117 moral duty provision — court can order provision for children if testator failed in moral duty

claimDeadlineMonths.description: 6 months from first extraction of grant of probate

capitalAcquisitionsTax.description: Capital Acquisitions Tax (CAT) thresholds — Irish equivalent of inheritance tax
capitalAcquisitionsTax.$comment: CAT group → kinship type mapping: Group A (€335,000 threshold): parent_child_biological, parent_child_adopted, grandparent_grandchild (minor grandchild of predeceased child only). Group B (€32,500): sibling, half_sibling, uncle_aunt, cousin, grandparent_grandchild (adult grandchild). Group C (€16,250): all others. These thresholds make kinship classification directly relevant to tax calculation.

probateProcess.description: Irish probate process — Probate Office or District Probate Registry

inlandRevenueAffidavit.description: Whether Revenue Commissioners affidavit (Form SA.2) filed

enduringPowerOfAttorney.description: Irish EPA — different from English LPA. Must be registered with the court before it can be used.

intestacyRules.description: Distribution order under Part VI of the Succession Act 1965

dwellingHouseExemption.description: CAT Section 86 dwelling house exemption — inherited home exempt if beneficiary lived there 3+ years prior and continues 6 years after

civilPartnershipProvisions.description: Civil Partnership and Certain Rights and Obligations of Cohabitants Act 2010

qualifiedCohabitant.description: 5 years cohabitation or 2 years with dependent child

section56Advancement.description: Advancement provisions under Section 56 of the Succession Act 1965 — lifetime gifts to children brought into account on intestacy

localTenureTypes.description: Maps each property to its local Irish tenure. The core property tenureType holds the territory-neutral value (ownership, lease); this records the local term
localTenureTypes.$comment: freehold: fee simple, the only legal freehold estate since the Land and Conveyancing Law Reform Act 2009. leasehold: a term of years, including long leases at a ground rent that the Landlord and Tenant (Ground Rents) Acts let the lessee buy out. fee_farm_grant: a fee simple subject to a perpetual rent; the 2009 Act stops new ones being created, but existing grants continue and still turn up on title. Ireland has no commonhold: apartments are held on long leases, with the common areas owned by an owners' management company under the Multi-Unit Developments Act 2011.

landRegistration.description: Which Irish register each property's title is recorded on, and with what class of title. Land Registry (Tailte Éireann) registers title in folios; unregistered title is evidenced by deeds recorded in the Registry of Deeds (Tailte Éireann)
landRegistration.$comment: Ireland runs two registers. Registration of Title Act 1964: title registered in a folio, guaranteed by the State, in one of the classes in titleClass (good_leasehold applies to leasehold folios only). Registration of Deeds and Title Act 2006: unregistered title, where the deeds are the title and the Registry of Deeds records them (by memorial for older deeds, by application form under the current rules). First registration has been compulsory on every sale throughout the State since 2011, so much property is still on the Registry of Deeds until it next changes hands. folioNumber and titleClass apply only to land_registry; deedsReference only to registry_of_deeds.

register.description: land_registry: title registered in a folio at the Land Registry (Tailte Éireann). registry_of_deeds: unregistered title, with deeds recorded in the Registry of Deeds (Tailte Éireann)

folioNumber.description: Land registry folio number, including the county prefix

titleClass.description: Class of title registered on the folio

deedsReference.description: Registry of Deeds reference — the serial number, or year, book and number for an older memorial

retrievedAt.description: When this registration data was retrieved or last verified

legislativeChanges.description: Tracked changes to Irish succession legislation
